#731. Judge Torn on Lil Durk Bail Question After Murder-for-Hire Verdict: ‘A Question of Psychology’

The rapper's lawyers want him out of jail ahead of a second racketeering trial. Prosecutors say he'll flee.

A judge is struggling with whether to let out Lil Durk on bail following his acquittal on murder-for-hire charges but before a second racketeering trial.

The “All My Life” hitmaker (Durk Banks) was found not guilty in September of taking out a hit on rival rapper Quando Rondo. Durk’s lawyers are now pushing for his release after more than two years in jail, offering to put up all his future music royalties as bond and even getting letters of support from Jay-Z and J. Cole.

Judge Michael W. Fitzgerald weighed the request during a Wednesday (Nov. 4) court hearing, attended by Billboard. The judge was torn, given that Durk attempted to flee to Dubai before his original 2024 arrest and still faces another trial next summer for allegedly operating his Only the Family (OTF) label as a violent gang.

On the one hand, Judge Fitzgerald said “not that much has changed” for Durk and that “even an innocent person would be tempted to flee” at this point. On the other, however, he noted that Durk “has a very strong incentive now to let the legal system play out, so the acquittals really do change the calculation a great deal.”

“It’s a question of psychology,” said the judge. “Would he flee?”

Durk’s team says the answer is no. His attorney Drew Findling argued Wednesday that the rapper “understands how the system works” and wants a second jury to find him not guilty again. Fellow defense lawyer Christy O’Connor also pointed out that the proposed bond package truly encompasses all his future earnings on his music, so he would be left destitute if he went on the lam.

Prosecutors want Durk to stay in jail. Assistant U.S. Attorney Daniel Weiner said Durk has “absolutely no respect for authority” and would “run amok” if let out. Weiner also pointed out that Durk could simply flee to a non-extradition country and make new music. “He could accumulate more wealth,” said the prosecutor.

Judge Fitzgerald ultimately took the bail motion under submission and will issue a written ruling in due course.

Durk was acquitted of murder-for-hire following a two-week trial, in which prosecutors accused him of putting a bounty on Rondo in retaliation for the 2020 killing of his close friend and collaborator King Von. Rondo was shot at a Los Angeles gas station in 2022 and survived, but his cousin Saviay’a Robinson, also known as Lul Pab, was killed in the crossfire.

The remaining count faced by Durk is under the federal Violent Crimes in Aid of Racketeering Activity (VICAR) statute, which broadly criminalizes gang violence. Prosecutors want to argue at next year’s second trial that Durk used his leadership role in OTF to orchestrate the Rondo incident, as well as a 2019 shooting in Atlanta and another 2022 killing in Chicago.

Durk’s attorneys say the VICAR count is “incredibly weak” and that everything related to the Rondo shooting should be excluded under double-jeopardy rules. This is a complex legal question that the attorneys will litigate in court papers over the next several months.

From Saturn's spectacular rings to Halloween fireballs and a space station flyover, there are plenty of celestial treats in store this Halloween. Here's when and where to look.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

There could be more than just ghosts and ghouls lurking in the skies this Halloween! From Saturn's spectacular rings to shooting stars and even a space station flyover, the night sky has a few treats of its own in store for U.S. skywatchers on Oct. 31.

Based on the latest national forecast, skies will be mainly clear on Saturday evening over most of New York State, northeast Pennsylvania, northern New Jersey and New England as well as a swath of the southern and central Great Plains, central Rockies, a portion of the Pacific Northwest and central and south Florida, as costumed kids arrive at the door looking for candy or some other Halloween treat.

Temperatures will be mostly in the chilly 40s across the Northeast US, upper 50s and 60s for the nation's midsection, warm 70s to near 80 for the southern US, including Florida and the Gulf Coast, and 40s for much of the western US. Unfortunately, a storm moving across the nation's heartland may spell rainy skies for parts of Iowa and Nebraska, south to the Gulf Coast.

For those blessed with a generally fair evening, there will be views of mid-autumn stars and constellations plus a bright planet shining prominently in the early evening sky. If you plan to accompany children around your neighborhood, you might want to enlighten them by pointing out some of those objects that will be visible in the sky. Better yet, if you have a telescope, give your visitors a treat of a different kind: Give them a close-up view of some of those celestial sights.

At around 7 p.m. local time, tell your young audience to make a clenched fist with their hands and then hold them out at arm's length. Now, tell them to go "two fists" up from the east-southeast horizon and they will see a bright star, shining with a yellow-white hue. Now, direct your telescope toward that "star" and when you gaze through the eyepiece, you will not be looking at a star at all . . . but a planet!

This sixth planet out from the sun, just might be the most beautiful of all. Its rings are still readily evident, although currently they appear somewhat edge-on with the south face tilted only about 6 and a half degrees to our line of sight. A telescope magnifying 30-power will bring them out; they appear to bisect the ball of the planet. While this is far from their appearance compared to other years, the view should still look impressive to those who have never seen the ringed planet for themselves.

Because they are active over Halloween, the Taurid meteor shower is sometimes called the "Halloween Fireballs." The bits of debris that make up the Taurids are a little larger than average, so they can result in brighter meteors and even fireballs, or exploding meteors (called bolides), that streak across the sky and leave incandescent trains in their wake. While they are most active during the second week of November, a few forerunners can show up on Halloween night, darting from out of the east-northeast part of the sky. So, if you or your young visitors see something resembling a flare from a Roman candle sweeping majestically across the evening sky, it may very well be a Taurid meteor.

Not the International Space Station, but the Tianhe-1 core module, the first module to launch of the Tiangong space station. It was launched into orbit on 29 April 2021, as the first launch of the final phase of the Tiangong program, part of the China Manned Space Program (Project 921). On Halloween evening, Tianhe-1 will be following a track from Chicago to New York at an altitude of 240 miles (385 km) and should be readily visible to the naked eye across the Northeast US within a few minutes of 7 p.m. EDT, wherever skies are reasonably clear.

The Tiangong Space Station should appear to resemble a very bright star moving across the sky on a general west-to-east course. For places near and along the flight path, the Space Station will appear to pass almost directly overhead. For those situated south of the track, Tiangong will reach its highest point above the northern horizon; those situated north of the track will see the station peak high in the south.

If you see it, tell your young viewers that three astronauts are currently living and working aboard the Tiangong Space Station, of which the Tianhe core module serves as the main living quarters. If you would like specific details on when and where to see the Space Station from your hometown, check out Heavens-Above, a non-profit website and mobile application that tracks satellites, the International Space Station (ISS), comets, and astronomical events in real time.

Another website that provides live information, including an orbit map on Tianhe-1, is NY2O.com. Check its menu list on the right side of the page and look for the blue box: "10-Day Predictions for CSS (Tianhe-1)."

In the September 2019 issue of The Astronomical League Magazine "Reflector," author Richard W. Schmude Jr., offered some tips for those who plan to do public outreach for astronomy on Halloween:

"Firstly, children sometimes grab or touch the eyepiece, so use an inexpensive one. I gently warn children not to touch the telescope. In my area, parents have learned to tell their children not to touch the telescope. In some cases, a child will grab the eyepiece, causing the telescope to shift. For this reason, a Dobsonian telescope with a good finderscope is a good choice for Halloween outreach. A small stool or booster ladder may help very small viewers. Sometimes, parents hold their children up to look through the eyepiece. One may also place a monitor-connected video camera in the telescope and people can easily see the object on a screen." "Finally," adds Mr. Schmude, "I have my bag of goodies next to my telescope so that the children get two treats!"

Whatever your weather, Happy Halloween from all of us at Space.com!

#727. Charles F. Porter, Actor and ‘Finding Faith’ Producer, Dies at 47

The former Duke football standout also made films for BET+, championed inspirational, independent cinema, wrote poetry and mentored kids.

Charles Porter, who produced Finding Faith, a 2025 film that starred starring Paula Patton, Loretta Devine and Keith David, and served as an advocate for inspirational independent filmmaking, has died. He was 47.

Porter died Monday at his home in Calabasas after a 17½-year battle with Hodgkin lymphoma, his family told The Hollywood Reporter.

As an actor, Porter appeared on TV series including The Parkers, House, Without a Trace and Bones and starred as the pioneering Black NASCAR driver Wendell Scott in the 2011 ESPN film Wendell Scott: A Race Story. Related Stories TV Former 'Ellen' Executive Producer Matthew Wright Dies as Ellen DeGeneres Posts Tearful Video Calling Him "The Glue to Our Entire Family" Music Marty Erlichman, Barbra Streisand's Longtime Manager, Dies at 97

As founder of Black Bench Productions, Porter developed, packaged, produced and financed indie films, championing stories of faith, family, resilience and redemption while creating opportunities for Black artists and filmmakers.

He was the guiding force behind Finding Faith, written and directed by LazRael Lison. The film, produced in collaboration with Summer House Pictures and Third Eye Productions, was released in theaters through Fathom Entertainment before running on Lifetime.

For BET+, Porter produced A Miracle Before Christmas (2022), starring David, LeToya Luckett and Romeo Miller, and Christmas Angel (2023), starring Miller, DaniLeigh, Skyh Black, Elise Neal and Tamar Braxton. Those were produced in collaboration with Summer House as well.

His other producing credits included the thrillers Nailed (2006), Battered (2014) — he also starred in those two — and Grace Point (2023).

Charles Frederick Porter II was born on March 13, 1979, in Oxford, England (his father was in the Air Force, and his mother is British). He came to the U.S. at age 3 and attended Rumsey Hall, a prep school in Washington Depot, Connecticut, and The Lawrenceville School in New Jersey.

He went on to Duke University, where he earned a degree in Cultural Anthropology and, at 6-foot-4 and 250 pounds, was a four-year football letterman as one of the ACC’s top defensive tackles. (A back injury ultimately ended his goal of playing pro ball.)

Porter moved to Los Angeles in 2002 and appeared on the ESPN game/reality show Beg, Borrow & Deal. In addition to his TV acting gigs, he also appeared in films including Holla (2006), Johnny Was (2006) and Peppermint (2018).

Porter was an executive producer and early investor on Last Meals, an upcoming feature from Sentient Entertainment and HanWay Films that stars Mads Mikkelsen, Boyd Holbrook, Tessa Thompson and Michael Shannon. He was developing a slate of faith-based films at the time of his death.

Porter also was a successful model, appearing in Italian Vogue, starring in an international Adidas campaign and walking the runway for the Ebony Fashion Fair. And as an author, he published three poetry books — Get to Know, Choose Your Path and Enjoying the Journey — and was working on B+, inspired by his changed blood type following one of his three bone marrow transplants.

He and his wife of 18 years, Candice Tab Porter, expressed their gratitude to the City of Hope and Dr. Stephen J. Forman “for their dedication and compassionate care.”

Away from Hollywood, Porter was a beloved youth football coach, personal trainer and mentor in Malibu, Calabasas and Westlake Village and the founder of Brainwashed for Greatness, dedicated to positivity and personal growth.

In addition to his wife, an entertainment marketing executive and former Hollywood publicist, survivors include daughters Layla Rose Porter, 9, and Juliette Jasmine Porter, 6; mother Dorothy Fourmeax; brother Sydney Sparks-Fourmeax; sister Natalie Zore; mother-in-law Jeeny Miller; sister-in-law and producing partner Renée Tab; brothers-in-law Amir Tab and Chris Tuffin; and nephews Alexander and Tristan Tuffin and Kayla, Phillip and Austin Zore.

His wife, sister-in-law and best friend and former Duke teammate, William L. Hill, were with him when he died. His guiding philosophy, his family said, remained constant: “Never Quit.”

"This companion is orbiting so close to the star that it actually passes through its extended atmosphere."

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Something spooky is stirring in the shadows of the infamous star Betelgeuse, a cosmic poltergeist that is disrupting the atmosphere of the red supergiant.

New radio observations have shown Betelgeuse's smaller stellar companion, Siwarha (not Betelguese Betelguese, unfortunately), cutting through the supergiant's extended atmosphere and leaving a wake in its path, like a jet boat slicing through a lake.

Because the name of this red supergiant star located about 650 light-years away from Earth, marking the shoulder of constellation Orion, is Betelgeuse, which means "the hand of al-Jawza" in Arabic, the companion was named Siwarha, meaning "her bracelet."

"This companion is orbiting so close to the star that it actually passes through its extended atmosphere," Lynn Matthews, the principal research scientist at Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) Haystack Observatory who led the new observations, said in a statement.

Using data collected from 2021 to 2026 using the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array in New Mexico and the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) in Chile, Matthews and colleagues found that Betelgeuse's atmosphere stretches into an egg shape when the companion star is farthest away and rounds out when the companion passes in front of or behind it.

The same data also showed that Betelgeuse itself has largely recovered from the "Great Dimming" that made headlines in 2020. This recovery comes after the red supergiant "sneezed" in 2020, dramatically ejecting tons of gas and dust and fading to its dimmest in more than a century.

Among the long-standing mysteries of Betelgeuse, scientists have puzzled over a brightening and dimming cycle that lasts roughly 2,100 days. Recent studies pointed to a low-mass companion orbiting deep inside the star's atmosphere, and its existence was confirmed in early 2026.

Though Siwarha itself is too faint to detect directly at radio wavelengths, its influence shows up in the star's shape, the new study found. To confirm the effect, the researchers say, they will need to observe more of the companion's orbit, especially at radio frequencies that have so far been sparsely sampled.

The Next Generation Very Large Array, a planned telescope, should make this kind of monitoring far more routine, according to the team. With sharper vision, researchers could see how red supergiants like Betelgeuse shed their material as they near the end of their lives, and how a close companion might affect that process by tugging on that ejected matter.

This research is described in a paper published in The Astronomical Journal.

Sharmila Kuthunur is an independent space journalist based in Bengaluru, India. Her work has also appeared in Scientific American, Science, Astronomy and Live Science, among other publications. She holds a master's degree in journalism from Northeastern University in Boston.

#725. The $1.4 Billion ‘No-Brainer’ Opportunity The Music Industry Is Missing

Soundtrack, the music streamer used by restaurants and retailers globally, estimates billions are lost in revenue every year in the U.S. from businesses that unwittingly stream music illegally.

By Elizabeth Dilts Marshall

While music industry leaders discuss superfan monetization and craft economic models for AI music applications that don’t yet exist, Ola Sars, founder and head of Soundtrack, says they are missing out on $1.4 billion in royalties that go uncollected in the United States every year from businesses illegally playing copyrighted music.

That’s according to a new study released Thursday (Nov. 5) by Soundtrack, a commercial music streaming platform backed by Spotify that is now used by 60,000 businesses in 75 countries. Related Kenny MacPherson, Veteran Music Publisher and Big Deal Music Co-Founder, Dies at 71 Jessica Lynch

The independent study, which Soundtrack commissioned, surveyed around 1,500 representatives of some 15,000 U.S. business locations and found that only 19% of those that play music are fully compliant with commercial music requirements. Nearly 80% of U.S. businesses use consumer streaming services, which are only licensed for personal use, to play music in-store, and just 5% reported having licenses from all four major performing rights organizations (PROs): ASCAP, BMI, GMR and SESAC.

At a time when the revenue growth from subscription and ad-supported streaming is slowing, Sars says the music industry could “unlock exponential growth” in the money it collects from U.S. businesses by turning their attention to this “extreme” level of non-compliance.

“People are playing music already, but they simply don’t know that it’s not licensed for commercial use. They haven’t read the terms and no one has told them,” Sars tells Billboard. “It is what you guys in the U.S. would call a pretty big no-brainer. If you’re playing music in your business, artists should be fairly compensated. There is a rate structure in place, and you can’t use a personal service in your business. But it’s complicated.”

Commercial music streaming in businesses can be the next growth area in music, Sars says. Soundtrack says it recently partnered with SESAC to round out its pitch to U.S. businesses.

Based in Sweden, Soundtrack generates roughly 60 million euros ($67 million) in annual recurring revenue and is on track to generate $100 million by 2028. Previously called Soundtrack Your Brand, the company raised $15 million in 2023 from investors like Matt Pincus’ MUSIC and Dundee Partners, who joined existing investors Balderton Capital, Fuel Venture Capital, Industrifonden, Telia, DIG and Matt Spetzler.

“Ultimately, our aim is to create a healthy ecosystem for the background music industry by growing the ‘pie’ for music creators and rights-holders, while not breaking the bank for hard-working businesses,” SARS says.

#724. Pixar Taps Jonathan Garson as President With Jim Morris Stepping Back to President Emeritus

Additionally, Jonas Rivera has been elevated to creative executive vp, while Pete Docter continues to lead the animation studio as chief creative officer.

Pixar Animation Studios is drawing up a plan for its next leadership chapter.

Disney Entertainment co-chairman Alan Bergman announced Wednesday that Jonathan Garson will become Pixar’s new president, while longtime studio exec Jim Morris will transition to a president emeritus position. With Pete Docter continuing to lead Pixar as chief creative officer, Jonas Rivera moves into an expanded role as creative executive vp overseeing filmmakers and development and will work closely with Garson and Docter. The changes take effect Jan. 4, 2027. Related Stories General News Johnny Depp on His One Condition to Return as Jack Sparrow for 'Pirates of the Caribbean 6' TV A Royal Surprise: 'The Remarried Empress' Releases One Day Early on Disney+ and Hulu

In his new role, Garson will partner with Docter in overseeing all Pixar production and operations. In segueing to president emeritus, Morris continues as executive producer of Incredibles 3 and will also handle talent development at Pixar and Walt Disney Studios as a whole, along with focusing on technology initiatives. Both Garson and Morris will report to Bergman.

“Having worked closely with Jim Morris for more than 20 years, I have enormous respect for his leadership and unwavering commitment to Pixar and its people,” Bergman said in a statement. “He’s not only a tremendous partner in business but a great friend. As we prepare for his eventual retirement, this transition will ensure a smooth succession for the team.”

Bergman added, “With a deep background at both Pixar and Disney, Jonathan Garson has proven to be an exceptional leader with a strong sense of what makes Pixar unique and how its storytelling comes to life in so many ways for fans, and Pete Docter and I are excited for him to step into this role. In addition, Jonas Rivera brings a wealth of creative expertise that will serve the team well as he works even more closely with Pete.”

Having served as president for 12 years, Morris started his Pixar run in 2005 after a lengthy stint at Lucasfilm and ILM. Throughout Morris’ tenure, Pixar movies have surpassed $12 billion at the worldwide box office.

“Leading Pixar has been the privilege of a lifetime, and I’m honored to have been a steward of its legacy alongside extraordinary artists, storytellers, and technologists who keep redefining what animation can do and expanding the art of cinema,” Morris said. “After 52 years in the business, and almost 40 at Lucasfilm and Pixar, I’ll be stepping back from the day-to-day, but I’m thrilled to move into handling a number of special projects, working alongside my friends Pete, Jonathan and Jonas at Pixar, and of course Alan Bergman, who has been such a supporter of Pixar throughout the years.”

He continued, “Looking ahead, I can’t think of anyone better than Jonathan to carry the legacy of this beloved studio forward. He’s a Pixar person through and through, a fierce champion of our films, our people and our culture. Pixar is in very good hands.”

Garson has been with Disney for more than three decades and began his time with Pixar in 2010. He collaborated closely with Docter and Morris over the past 16 years, most recently serving as Pixar’s general manager after previously leading the marketing and franchise team.

“I still remember seeing Toy Story for the first time — never imagining I’d one day work at Pixar, let alone step into a leadership role such as this,” said Garson. “Every day I walk in the door here, I’m reminded just how special this place is and how lucky I am to be a part of it. Jim has shown me what it looks like to safeguard this culture of quality, innovation and creative ambition, and I’m extremely grateful to both him and Alan for their trust and support. It’s a humbling opportunity, and I look forward to working with Pete, Jonas, the production leadership team led by Katherine Sarafian and Lindsey Collins, and all of the extraordinary talent here at Pixar as we continue to push boundaries and lead our studio into the future.”

Rivera will partner with Docter in overseeing Pixar’s directors and creative vps, along with the development, casting and content advisement departments. Both Rivera and Docter will executive produce every Pixar feature. Rivera started at Pixar in 1994 and has since worked on nearly every release, with his accolades including Oscar wins for Inside Out and Toy Story 4.

“Ever since I walked through these doors as Pixar’s first production intern, this place, its people and its stories have been my life’s work,” said Rivera. “I am deeply honored to step into this new role alongside Pete, partnering with him and Jonathan to support our incredible filmmakers and artists. Jim has been an extraordinary mentor and leader, and I intend to build on the lessons I learned from him as we look toward our next chapter.”

Pixar’s latest release was this summer’s Toy Story 5, which crossed the billion-dollar mark globally and is expected to generate awards attention. The studio’s forthcoming features include next year’s Gatto, with Ghost Market and Incredibles 3 set for 2028.

The waning moon shines with Jupiter, Mars and the brilliant star Regulus in the eastern sky overnight Nov. 1-2.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The moon dives towards the glowing heart of the constellation Leo for a spectacular rendezvous with Mars and Jupiter overnight on Nov. 1-2, as the glittering stars of the Beehive Cluster shine nearby. Here's what you need to know.

Look to the eastern horizon an hour after midnight to see the 45%-lit waning moon shining less than 5 degrees from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length to the night sky.

Jupiter's bright light will gleam just below the red planet, with the bright star Regulus lining up beyond to form a dazzling procession leading back to the horizon. The stars of the Beehive Cluster (M44) can be found twinkling 10 degrees from the unlit side of the lunar disk around this time, in the middle of the constellation Cancer.

Stargazers in Australia, Indonesia and a host of other island nations and territories will see the moon pass directly in front of Jupiter, hiding its light in an event known as an occultation starting at 3:45 p.m. EST (2045 GMT) on Nov. 2 , according to In-The-Sky.org. However, the exact visibility and timings depend on location.

The cosmic pile-up serves as a spectacular reminder of the scale and diversity of targets on display in the night sky. After all, the moon appears largest from our Earthly perspective, but in reality it's less than half the diameter of Mars.

Jupiter, meanwhile, is over 20 times wider than the red planet, while mighty Regulus is up to four times larger than the sun, andcould easily fit all the planets of the solar system in its vast expanse.

By moonrise on the night of Nov. 3, the lunar crescent will have leapt past Jupiter and Mars, to appear just 1 degree from the blue-white light of Regulus for viewers in the U.S. Meanwhile, viewers in several South American countries including Brazil, Peru, Argentina and Bolivia will see the moon occult Regulus beginning at 6:59 EST (1024 GMT) on Nov. 3. The exact timings for a selection of South American countries can be found below, courtesy of In-The-Sky.org.

Want to get a closer look at the moon and planets of the solar system? Then be sure to check out our picks of the best telescopes and binoculars for exploring the night sky, including the Celestron NexStar 8SE, which we rank as the best motorized telescope out there.
